Subject: Onboarding: international transfers & documentation

Hi Evelyn / Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthBridge is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our triage workflows. Before we proceed with the pilot purchase order, our legal and procurement teams need a clear list of what Redwood can provide for cross-border processing. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation Redwood will sign the UK Addendum (IDTA) to the DPA and a redlineable template.
- A short inventory of subprocessors that may handle EU/UK-origin data and the regions where they operate.
- An evidence list for the TIA/DTIA (sample audit logs, KV cache retention policy, egress controls).
- Any proposed timeline to complete the evidence handoff so procurement can issue PO.

I've attached a short risk matrix our security team filled out (HealthBridge_RiskMatrix.pdf). Can you confirm owners on your side and a rough 2-week timeline?

Best,
Alicia Romero
Head of IT Procurement
HealthBridge Inc.

Subject: RE: Onboarding: international transfers & documentation — legal scope

Alicia / Team,

I've reviewed the risk matrix and sketched a pragmatic approach below. High-level summary first, then an evidence checklist and next steps.

High-level legal approach:
- We can sign the Redwood DPA with the UK Addendum (IDTA) in place; attaching a working template (UK_Addendum_Template_Redwood_v1.docx). We'll mark any commercial clauses (indemnity, liability caps) as out of scope for this redline — those remain in the main DPA/contract.
- For the TIA vs DTIA: operational evidence that HealthBridge is asking for aligns with a TIA (technical implementation assessment). We'll provide the scoped evidence package and are prepared to complete a DTIA where required but will need to sequence it after pilot telemetry.

Evidence checklist (what we'll provide):
- Subprocessor list with processing locations and contract dates (Subprocessor_Map_anon.csv).
- Sample audit log extract (redacted) showing request IDs, timestamps, and region metadata.
- KV/prefix caching retention and eviction policy document.
- Network egress controls and peering map for EU/UK regions.
- KMS architecture note (we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys; for HSM please confirm requirement).
- SOC 2 Type II report excerpt location and date.

Open questions for HealthBridge:
- Do you need live access to logs, or will a redacted export suffice for procurement/legal review?
- Please confirm whether subprocessors in APAC are in scope for your pilot.

Next steps and timeline:
- We will send UK addendum template with comments within 48 hours.
- Naomi will prepare an evidence package prototype (redacted logs + subprocessor CSV) within 5 business days.
- Mutual action plan to be agreed by 2026-11-20; evidence sprint to follow with a target of completion by 2026-12-04 if PO is executed week of 2026-11-22.

Quote: "On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 09:03 AM Alicia Romero <alicia.romero@healthbridge.com> wrote:"
> Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthBridge is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our triage workflows. Before we proceed with the pilot purchase order, our legal and procurement teams need a clear list of what Redwood can provide for cross-border processing.

Happy to hop on a short call if useful — I can be the primary redline owner.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RE: Onboarding: international transfers & documentation — legal scope

Kimberly / Evelyn,

Thanks for the template and the clarity on TIA sequencing. A couple of practical redline suggestions from HealthBridge counsel's perspective:

1) Add a short carveout in the UK Addendum that clarifies Redwood's fallback routing policies when EU/UK capacity is constrained and the impact on scope of processing under the addendum (helps procurement understand operational risk).
2) Confirm the retention window for the redacted audit export we will receive (HealthBridge needs at least 90 days of indexed logs for investigation).
3) For the subprocessor map: include a boolean column "transfers_outside_eu_uk" so we can filter for subject-to-TIA processors.

Also, HealthBridge has requested a DocuSign link to sign a preliminary mutual action plan once terms are agreed — sharing a placeholder here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/placeholder-signing-link

If Redwood can provide a redacted audit sample and the subprocessor CSV by 2026-11-19 we can keep the PO cadence intact.

Best regards,
Emma White
Partner, Jurisconsult LLP
(on behalf of HealthBridge legal)
